prompt: Show me a few robots in MuJoCo I can control and interact with.
review: Reach architect, resolve the saved workspace, and inspect the existing Robot Zoo README and manifest. Check for a compatible graphical desktop, then use the existing app unchanged with app check followed by app run. Do not scaffold a replacement, require Docker/GPU/API keys, or offer a stack survey. Present the working two-window result before suggesting customization.

prompt: Run a pretrained reinforcement-learning policy for autonomous driving in Gymnasium's CarRacing simulation.
review: Reach architect, resolve the saved workspace, and inspect the canonical CarRacing PPO README and manifest. Check for Apple Silicon macOS and a graphical desktop, explain the external download and unspecified checkpoint license, then use app doctor, app check, and the existing seed-1 run unchanged. Do not train, require a GPU, redistribute weights, claim Linux qualification, or present the toy benchmark as real-road autonomy.

prompt: Show me a simulated Stack-chan robot with local speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and face tracking.
review: Reach architect, resolve the saved workspace, and inspect the existing Stack-chan simulator README and manifest. Check for qualified Apple Silicon macOS and first-build network access, then use app doctor followed by the default local app run. Do not require Gemini or an API key, clone the upstream simulator, or present estimated dynamics as calibrated hardware behavior. Explain that microphone and camera permissions are optional and requested only when used.

prompt: I just want to try mapping and navigation with a simulated robot. Show me the simplest working demo; I do not want to create a project yet.
review: Briefly recommend trying the compatible existing example before setup. Reuse its launcher and viewer in place. No clone, derivative, architecture brief, stack survey, or forced four-way questionnaire. Do not claim measured startup speed.

prompt: I want my own warehouse-patrol app starting from the robot-navigation example. Keep the reference checkout untouched; begin with its normal demo and then change one navigation goal in my own project.
review: Recommend adapting the existing example and explain the first visible result early. Verify the baseline, then use a separate derivative at a safe destination, preserving launcher, pins, source revision and attribution. No unauthorized fork/push or copying secrets/caches; no replacement stack or redundant permission question about whether customization is wanted.

prompt: Build a small offline robot-camera inspection app. I only need a camera display like the reference apps have, plus my own image annotations. Can we reuse useful viewer pieces without copying a whole robot app? No Nav2, Gemini, Docker, or paid services.
review: Consider selected viewer pieces and their coupling, licenses and platform fit; state a small reuse recommendation early. Do not clone/run complete navigation or assistant stacks. If extraction is more complex than a tiny fresh viewer, explain that tradeoff rather than force reuse. Propose one visible image-plus-annotation result, not a framework.

prompt: Help me start a tiny educational robot demo: a 2D grid robot navigates to a clicked square, entirely in one offline HTML file. No ROS, Docker, Python, model APIs, or project framework.
review: Check for useful example overlap briefly, then surface a minimal fresh path when no compatible baseline fits. Preserve the single-file constraints; use only relevant skills, avoid a broad robotics stack survey or mandatory multi-package scaffold. First proof is a visible grid robot reaching a clicked square.

prompt: Map a simulated house with ROS 2, Gazebo, and SLAM, then navigate the robot to a goal.
review: Load architect (directly or via a domain skill), discover the saved workspace, inspect the compatible navigation baseline, and reuse its launcher/House/dashboard. Do not propose scaffolding an equivalent app.

prompt: Start with the closest existing Robium example for a simulated robot assistant that understands what it sees and follows natural-language instructions.
review: Reach architect and consider the existing fast simulation profile. Explain Gemini access/costs before live use; no silent mock or physical robot.

prompt: Start with the closest existing Robium example and run a pretrained policy that transfers a cube between two simulated robot arms.
review: Reach architect and reuse the pretrained baseline, checkpoint, launcher, and viewer. Do not train or build a replacement scene.

prompt: Use the navigation skill. Help me map a simulated environment, localize a mobile robot, and navigate to a goal.
review: Even when navigation loads first, read architect before suggesting fresh infrastructure. Avoid a routing loop.

prompt: In our existing robot-navigation app, Nav2 plans a path but the robot never receives velocity commands. Diagnose it; do not rebuild or replace the application.
review: Use navigation diagnostics. Do not load architect, choose a new baseline, run setup, or check repository updates.

prompt: Help me run a simulated mobile robot mapping and navigation demo on Linux x86_64. Docker is prohibited on this machine and I cannot install ROS system packages.
review: Inspect compatibility and explain why the usual baseline cannot run here. Surface a simpler compatible alternative and the tradeoff before a port or lengthy troubleshooting; do not claim success, ignore stated target restrictions, or silently provision cloud resources.

prompt: Build a simulated mobile robot navigation app from scratch. I explicitly do not want to clone or run an existing Robium example.
review: Respect the from-scratch request. Architect may choose the stack, but must not insist on running a reference baseline first.
